name: splitting-schemes
title: Operator-splitting schemes for PDE/particle coupling: Jacobi (fvsolver), Gauss–Seidel, Strang

question:
The embedded vcell-fvsolver hard-codes one lagged (Jacobi-type) splitting. With the
coupling expressed as process-bigraph processes, can other splittings be used, and how
much accuracy do they buy at a given coupling interval?
hypothesis:
Jacobi and both Gauss–Seidel orderings are first order in the coupling interval τ.
Symmetric Strang splitting (half the PDE substeps, the particle step, the other half) is
second order in the mean dynamics and much more accurate at large τ.
description:
HybridCoupler composes the same FVReactionDiffusion and SmoldynHybrid engines and only
orders their substeps. Its jacobi scheme reproduces the two-process composite with
coupling="fvsolver" exactly (same seeds give identical counts; regression test in
tests/test_hybrid_cosim.py).

variants.name: splitting-scheme-sweep
variants.diff_from_baseline: Same engines, re-ordered substeps: Jacobi (fvsolver), Gauss–Seidel (particles-first and pde-first), symmetric Strang.

variants.name: coupling-interval-sweep
variants.diff_from_baseline: τ = k·Δt with k ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16, 32} at Δt = 0.005 s; 64 seeds per point; orders fitted for k ≥ 4.

simulation_set.name: default
simulation_set.description: 4 splitting schemes × 5 coupling intervals × 64 seeds; results/metrics.json.

behavior_tests.name: jacobi-first-order
behavior_tests.description: Fitted order of the Jacobi (fvsolver) scheme.

provenance.note: Explicit lagged splitting is first order.

behavior_tests.name: strang-much-more-accurate
behavior_tests.description: Strang error / Jacobi error at the largest coupling interval (k = 32, τ = 0.16 s).

provenance.note: Symmetric splitting cancels the leading splitting error.

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-03):
- **First-order schemes:** Jacobi (fvsolver) has order 1.23, Gauss–Seidel orders are
  1.01 and 1.08. At τ = 0.16 s their errors are about 0.021–0.023.
- **Strang:** the error stays within about 2× of the sampling floor (4–11·10⁻⁴) for every
  τ up to 0.16 s, 25× smaller than Jacobi at τ = 0.16 s. It is too close to the floor to
  fit an order; more seeds or larger τ would resolve it.
- **Consequence:** for this model, Strang splitting lets the particle side step about 32×
  less often than the PDE side at roughly the accuracy fvsolver's scheme reaches with
  k ≈ 1–2. That's a large potential speed-up for particle-dominated runs (A6).
  vcell-fvsolver's hybrid loop (SimTool.cpp) fixes one splitting order, so adopting
  Strang there would mean modifying the solver; here it is a coupler option.

findings.statement: All three lagged splittings are first order in the coupling interval τ: the fitted order is 1.23 for Jacobi (fvsolver), 1.01 for Gauss–Seidel (particles-first) and 1.08 for Gauss–Seidel (pde-first). At τ = 0.16 s their errors cluster at 2.1–2.3% (Jacobi 0.0218, GS-particles 0.0208, GS-pde 0.0226).
findings.next_action: None — first-order behaviour confirmed for all lagged schemes.

findings.statement: Symmetric Strang splitting is dramatically more accurate at large coupling interval: at k = 32 (τ = 0.16 s) the Strang error is 0.000859, 3.94% of the Jacobi error (b3_strang_over_jacobi_err_k32 = 0.0394, i.e. a 25× reduction), well under the 0.25 acceptance band. Expressing the coupling as process-bigraph substeps makes this re-ordering a coupler option rather than a solver modification.
findings.next_action: Exploit in particle-dominated runs (A6): Strang lets the particle side step ~32× less often than the PDE side at the accuracy Jacobi reaches near k ≈ 1–2.

findings.statement: Strang's error stays within ~2× of the sampling floor across the whole sweep (0.000405 at k=2 to 0.000859 at k=32), so its fitted order (0.34) is floor-dominated and not resolvable — more seeds or larger τ would be needed to measure the expected second order.
findings.next_action: Add more seeds or extend τ to resolve the Strang convergence order.

regression_compatibility.basis: results/metrics.json is committed and regenerated by sims/run.py; the Jacobi scheme reproduces the fvsolver two-process composite exactly (regression test in tests/test_hybrid_cosim.py). All three behavior tests pass against the committed metrics.

biological_validation.basis: Not a biological claim — this is a numerical-methods study of operator-splitting accuracy for the PDE/particle coupling against the continuum survival curve.

explanatory_gain.basis: F-02 shows the process-bigraph decomposition unlocks a splitting (Strang) the embedded fvsolver cannot express, buying a 25× accuracy gain at the largest coupling interval.

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: Lagged splittings (Jacobi, Gauss–Seidel) are first order and Strang is far more accurate at large τ (25× smaller error at k=32) — adopt Strang as a coupler option for particle-dominated runs; resolve the Strang order with more seeds / larger τ.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: A fitted Jacobi order outside [0.7, 1.5], or a Strang/Jacobi ratio ≥ 0.25 at k=32, would mean the splitting substeps are mis-ordered or the sampling floor was mis-estimated — re-check build_coupler_document and the seed count before trusting the accuracy claim.

report.caveat: Strang's fitted order (0.34) is sampling-floor-dominated and does not resolve its expected second order; the accuracy claim rests on the error ratio, not the fitted order.

rerun.note: Full sweep (4 splitting schemes × 5 coupling intervals × 64 seeds). Deterministic per seed; the Jacobi scheme matches the fvsolver two-process composite exactly.
